newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bond prices fell sharply, undermined by firmer Swiss franc short-term interest rates.

A Swiss National Bank spokesman said the central bank's policy was unchanged, adding that Swiss short-term rates often move inversely to the Swiss franc. In Asian trade Wednesday, the dollar rose to 1.2725 Swiss francs, its highest level since late May.

Swiss franc swap rates were also up significantly, with shorter rates rising relative to long rates. Two-year swaps were quoted midday up 17 basis points, at 2.30/38, but were seen off highs by late afternoon.
Traders said the market was nervous after call money rose above 1-1/2 percent. Rates up to one year were also higher. The rise follows an SNB discount rate on September 26.
"We are hearing some nervousness as to why the money market rates (with maturities of three months and over) should follow the short dates up," one trader said.

But few traders believe the SNB will tighten so soon after lowering rates. Domestic money market traders attributed the tightness to technical factors before the end of the bank maintenance period on October 19. One London-based trader said some of the drop in Euro-Swiss may simply be a correction.
Traders said the Swiss bond futures and cash market followed swaps, with 10-year rates rising 13 basis points which equated roughly to the rise in 10-year yields.
Dec Comi medium-term bond down 70 at 109.90.
Dec Euro Swiss francs down 15 at 98.15.
